content.value_statement: Large parallel workloads need careful Azure Batch setup. This skill guides Java developers through clients, pools, jobs, tasks, monitoring, and cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Lists the Maven dependency and Azure Batch prerequisites.
Shows Java client creation with Microsoft Entra ID and shared key credentials.
Explains pool creation, resizing, autoscale, and deletion patterns.
Covers job, task, node, and job schedule operations.
Demonstrates task output retrieval and Batch error handling.
Links to package, SDK, API, product, REST, and sample resources.
limitations: It does not create Azure resources or run code by itself.
The documented package version is a beta release.
Examples use placeholder resource names and account values.
It does not cover full RBAC, networking, quota, or compliance design.

use_cases.title: Create a Batch Client
use_cases.description: Generate Java setup steps for authenticating to Azure Batch with Microsoft Entra ID.

use_cases.title: Operate Batch Pools
use_cases.description: Plan pool creation, resizing, autoscale, and deletion for cloud compute workloads.

use_cases.title: Run Parallel Tasks
use_cases.description: Design jobs and task collections for large parallel processing workloads.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to create an Azure Batch Java client with Microsoft Entra ID and an endpoint from environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Create and Resize a Pool
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft Java steps to create an Ubuntu Batch pool, resize it, wait for completion, and explain each required parameter.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Job With Many Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Java Azure Batch job with retry limits, wall clock limits, and one thousand generated tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Batch Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure Batch Java workflow for authentication, autoscale, task output retrieval, cleanup, and production readiness.

output_examples.input: Create a pool for two Ubuntu compute nodes and connect with Java.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan covering Maven setup, Entra ID authentication, pool parameters, node counts, and long-running operation handling.

output_examples.input: Explain how to submit many tasks and collect standard output.
output_examples.output: A task workflow describing batch submission, task listing, file retrieval, output decoding, and error checks.

output_examples.input: Review my planned Azure Batch cleanup process.
output_examples.output: A checklist for job termination, pool deletion, output retention, retry settings, and cost controls.

best_practices: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID over shared key credentials for production use.
Set task constraints, retry limits, and cleanup steps before scaling jobs.
Confirm pool size, autoscale formulas, and low-priority node impact before large runs.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real access keys into prompts, examples, or logs.
Do not run unreviewed task command lines on Batch nodes.
Do not delete pools or jobs before confirming output retention requirements.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps build Java workflows for Azure Batch clients, pools, jobs, tasks, nodes, and schedules.

faq.question: Does it run Azure Batch jobs directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that you review and run in your own environment.

faq.question: Which authentication method is recommended?
faq.answer: Microsoft Entra ID is recommended. Shared key credentials are shown only as an alternative pattern.

faq.question: Can it help with task output?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers retrieving task files and reading standard output from completed tasks.

faq.question: Is the SDK version stable?
faq.answer: The source references version 1.0.0-beta.5, so confirm the current package version before production use.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
